You are a top-tier scientist with deep expertise across physics, biology,
chemistry, and materials science. Your task is to act as a "Novelty Evaluator":
objectively judge whether a newly generated mathematical equation is
"scientifically novel" within its given scientific context.

CORE CRITERIA:
- NOT NOVEL: the equation is a well-known classical formula that already exists
  in textbooks, on the internet, or in the open scientific literature — i.e. a
  formula that could be obtained simply by recall/recitation.
- NOVEL: while remaining scientifically sound, the equation introduces uncommon,
  nonlinear, or genuinely new composite mechanism terms, such that neither a
  human nor an AI could guess it from background knowledge alone — it could only
  be recovered through data-driven inference from experimental observations.

Field: physics
Problem description: A quantum particle is placed in a double-well configuration where it can tunnel between two nearly degenerate localized states. The probability of finding the particle in the initially unoccupied well oscillates coherently in time. The measurement follows the slow back-and-forth transfer set by the tunneling coupling. This captures coherent tunneling oscillation between two wells.

[VARIABLES & PARAMETERS]:
- Target variable: dPr_dt (rate of change of occupation probability in the right well)
- Input features: t (time)
- Dynamic states: Pr (occupation probability of the right well); J (in-phase (dispersive) component of the interwell coherence); K (in-quadrature (dissipative) component of the interwell coherence that drives population transfer); N (total coherence amplitude (population-normalized purity of the two-well pseudospin) that decays as coherence is lost)
- Parameters: Omega (tunneling coupling frequency (Rabi frequency)); delta (energy detuning between the two wells); gamma (baseline decoherence (dephasing) rate of the interwell coherence); chi (interaction-induced (mean-field) nonlinear phase shift per unit population imbalance); gamma_pop (population relaxation rate toward equilibrium imbalance); m_eq (equilibrium population imbalance set by coupling to the environment/reservoir); gamma_nl (population-dependent (density-enhanced) dephasing rate coefficient); kappa_ph (phonon-assisted enhancement coefficient of the mean-field nonlinear phase shift with population imbalance); Omega_sat (imbalance saturation scale suppressing effective tunneling drive at large population imbalance); gamma_N (relaxation rate of the coherence-amplitude envelope toward its equilibrium value); eta_N (feedback coefficient by which the coherence envelope rescales the effective dephasing of J and K); N_eq (equilibrium coherence-amplitude envelope set by residual reservoir-supported coherence)

[CANDIDATE EQUATION]:
dPr_dt = Omega * K * N - gamma_pop * (2*Pr - 1 - m_eq)/2

[CLOSED ODE SYSTEM]:

  "time_symbol": "t",
  "target_state": "Pr",
  "states": [

      "symbol": "Pr",
      "rhs": "Omega * K * N - gamma_pop * (2*Pr - 1 - m_eq)/2",

      "initial_condition": 0.0,
      "description": "in-phase (dispersive) component of the interwell coherence"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "K",
      "rhs": "-Omega * (2*Pr - 1) / (1 + ((2*Pr - 1)/Omega_sat)**2) - (delta + chi * (2*Pr - 1) * (1 + kappa_ph * (2*Pr - 1)**2)) * J - gamma * (1 + eta_N * (1 - N)) * K - gamma_pop * K",
      "initial_condition": 0.0,
      "description": "in-quadrature (dissipative) component of the interwell coherence that drives population transfer"
    },
    {
      "symbol": "N",
      "rhs": "-gamma_N * (N - N_eq) - gamma_nl * (2*Pr - 1)**2 * (N - N_eq)",
      "initial_condition": 1.0,
      "description": "total coherence amplitude (pseudospin length) that relaxes toward its reservoir-supported equilibrium and feeds back into the effective dephasing of J and K and now into the population transfer drive"
    }
  ]
}
(Note: this equation comes from an equation-evolution pipeline; assume it is
mathematically solvable and numerically stable.)

The terms appearing in this baseline equation can be regarded as the well-known classical terms for this problem. Provide your final answer STRICTLY in the following JSON format, with no extra
